newsitem.title: INDIA: INDIA'S KHURANA QUITS BJP POST IN PROTEST.
newsitem.headline: INDIA'S KHURANA QUITS BJP POST IN PROTEST.

text.p: Madan Lal Khurana, former chief minister of Delhi, said on Friday that he had resigned as vice president of India's Hindu nationalist Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) following differences with the party chief.

Senior leaders of the BJP, India's main opposition group, decided on Thursday against reinstating Khurana as Delhi's chief minister, a post he quit last year after facing bribery charges in a $18-million "hawala" or illegal foreign exchange scandal.
In May, a Delhi court cleared Khurana of the charges in the scandal in which 100 politicians were implicated. The charges were based on entries made in a foreign exchange dealer's diary.
"The court has cleared me but you still consider me an accused," Khurana said in a letter to BJP president L.K. Advani.
"I resign from the post of vice presidentship of the party and as supervisor of Punjab and Rajasthan," he said, referring to two northwestern states.

"Loyalty to a political party is overdemanding," Khurana said in a statement. "Even unfairness and injustice has to be suffered. I am today a victim of this loyalty and I have decided to suffer its consequences."
Khurana said he would continue to serve the party as an ordinary worker.
